Bitwarden vs 1Password vs Keeper for emergency access (2026)

Short answer: Bitwarden and Keeper both have built-in emergency access; 1Password doesn't. Bitwarden lets trusted contacts request View or Takeover access after a wait time you set, with Premium listed at US$19.80 a year (checked 15 Oct 2026). Keeper allows up to 5 contacts with an optional delay of up to 3 months. 1Password relies on a printed Emergency Kit.

Key facts

  • Bitwarden: built-in emergency access; Premium US$19.80/yr (checked 15 Oct 2026)
  • Keeper: built-in emergency access; up to 5 contacts; optional delay up to 3 months
  • 1Password: no built-in emergency access; Emergency Kit

What do heirs actually do, step by step?

Bitwarden

  1. Your contact needs a free or paid Bitwarden account on the same server.
  2. They request View or Takeover access from their account.
  3. Access is granted when you approve it or when your wait time runs out.

Official site ↗

Keeper

  1. Your contact needs their own Keeper account.
  2. After the access delay you set (optional, up to 3 months), they can log in to your vault.
  3. Up to 5 contacts can be named.

Official site ↗

1Password

  1. There's no built-in emergency request.
  2. Your heir uses the Emergency Kit you left (sign-in address, email, Secret Key and password).
  3. On Families or business plans, an organiser can help recover a member's account.

Official site ↗

Frequently asked questions

Which has the best emergency access: Bitwarden, 1Password or Keeper?

Bitwarden, for most people: built-in requests, View or Takeover access, and a wait time you control. Keeper is a strong alternative. 1Password has no built-in emergency access.

How much does Bitwarden Premium cost?

Bitwarden's pricing page lists Premium at US$19.80 a year (checked 15 Oct 2026).

How many emergency contacts can I have?

Bitwarden: no limit stated. Keeper: up to 5. 1Password: anyone you give your Emergency Kit to.
